meta.name: Send critical NPM CVE alerts from GitHub to Slack via Apify

name: Actor 19A — NPM CVE Monitor → Critical Vulnerability → Slack Emergency Alert

parameters.content:
## Actor 19A — NPM CVE Monitor → Critical Vulnerability → Slack Emergency Alert

### How it works

This workflow runs every Monday morning to retrieve a repository’s package.json from GitHub, submit it to an Apify NPM CVE monitor, and fetch the resulting audit data. It categorises vulnerabilities by severity, checks whether any critical or high findings exist, and only then formats and sends an emergency Slack alert.

### Setup steps

- Configure the schedule trigger for the desired monitoring cadence and timezone.
- Set up GitHub access for the package.json request, including the correct repository owner, repository name, branch, file path, and any required GitHub token headers.
- Configure the Apify HTTP requests with a valid Apify API token, the correct CVE monitor actor endpoint, and dataset result URL handling.
- Connect Slack credentials and choose the emergency alert channel or user for the CVE notification.

### Customization

Adjust the severity threshold in the categorisation or IF logic, change the Slack message format, or point the GitHub request at a different repository or package manifest.

## Schedule and package fetch

Starts the weekly scan, retrieves package.json from GitHub, and prepares the manifest content for vulnerability auditing.

## Run vulnerability audit

Submits the prepared package data to the Apify CVE monitor and retrieves the audit results dataset.

## Evaluate severity threshold

Categorises returned vulnerabilities and checks whether any critical or high-severity issues require escalation.

## Send emergency alert

Formats the escalation message and posts the CVE emergency alert to Slack when the severity condition is met.
